Project VYOMVEER is an interactive 3D educational space adventure designed to give children the experience of being an astronaut. Instead of only reading about space, children can explore and learn through different missions in a fun and engaging way.

The application allows users to create their own astronaut avatar, customize their spacesuit and prepare for space missions. It also introduces resource management, where players learn the importance of oxygen, water, food and power during space travel. Children can choose between Moon and Mars adventures, explore their environments and complete different mission challenges.

details:
Project Details – VYOMVEER

VYOMVEER is an interactive 3D space adventure designed for children aged 7–12. The idea behind this project is to let children experience what it feels like to be an astronaut rather than simply learning about space from books.

The journey begins with creating an astronaut avatar and customizing the spacesuit. Children can then prepare for their missions, manage important spacecraft resources such as oxygen, water, food and power, and explore two different destinations – the Moon and Mars. Through different activities and mission challenges, they get an idea of how astronauts live, work and handle situations during space exploration.

One of the interesting parts of our project is resource management. Children can understand why essential resources are important and how their usage affects the mission. The Moon and Mars adventures also introduce them to different planetary environments in an interactive way.

The main benefit of VYOMVEER is that it combines entertainment with learning. It encourages curiosity, logical thinking, decision-making and problem-solving while making space science easier to understand. Our aim is to create a learning experience where children enjoy the adventure and gain scientific knowledge naturally.

We focused on making the application simple to use, visually engaging and suitable for young learners, so that exploring space feels like an adventure rather than a classroom lesson.
